chapterName: Middle Republic: The First Punic War (264-241 BCE)

questions.question: What makes the Battle of Cape Ecnomus in 256 BC stand out?
options: It was fought entirely at night
It was possibly the largest naval battle in history by combatants
It was the first battle with the corvus
It was Carthage's greatest naval victory
It ended the war
questions.explanation: With some 680 ships and up to 290,000 crew and marines, Ecnomus may be history's largest naval battle by number of combatants. Carthage lost 94 ships, Rome 24.
questions.sourceQuote: With some 680 ships and up to 290,000 crew and marines, it was possibly the largest naval battle in history by number of combatants.

questions.question: Whom did Carthage hire to retrain its army against Regulus?
options: A deserter from the Roman legions
An Egyptian general
A Spartan mercenary commander
An Athenian admiral
A Macedonian engineer
questions.explanation: A Spartan mercenary commander retrained Carthage's army. In 255 BC the retrained army crushed the Romans and captured Regulus.
questions.sourceQuote: Carthage hired a Spartan mercenary commander to retrain its army.

questions.question: Nearly bankrupt by 243 BC, how did Rome pay for its final war fleet?
options: By having its richest citizens each fund a warship
By melting down temple treasures
By borrowing money from Egypt
By selling captured Sicilians into slavery
By taxing its Italian allies heavily
questions.explanation: The Senate asked the richest Romans to fund a warship each, to be repaid from Carthage's future war payments. Egypt had refused Carthage a loan.
questions.sourceQuote: So the Senate asked the richest Romans each to fund a warship, to be repaid from Carthage's future war payments.

questions.question: During the siege of Akragas, what gave the garrison its chance to break into the Roman camp?
options: The Romans withdrew to meet a fleet
The Romans were celebrating a festival
A Roman consul fell ill
A storm destroyed the Roman siege works
Roman troops scattered to gather crops at harvest
questions.explanation: Feeding 40,000 men was hard while Carthage ruled the sea, so at harvest time the troops scattered for food. The garrison burst out but was driven back.
questions.sourceQuote: Feeding so many men was hard while Carthage ruled the sea, and at harvest time the troops scattered to gather crops.

questions.question: How did Rome's first homemade warships compare with the Carthaginian original they copied?
options: Larger and better armed
Smaller with fewer oarsmen
Lighter and faster
Heavier and slower
Identical in every respect
questions.explanation: Rome's novice shipwrights built 120 warships that were heavier and slower than the originals. Rowing a quinquereme in unison demanded long training.
questions.sourceQuote: Rome built 120 warships, but its novice shipwrights produced copies that were heavier and slower than the originals.

questions.question: Why do we have no Carthaginian account of the First Punic War?
options: Polybius burned them in Rome
They were lost in a shipwreck
Hamilcar destroyed them on leaving Sicily
They perished when Carthage was destroyed in 146 BC
Carthaginians never kept written records
questions.explanation: Carthage's records were lost when Rome destroyed the city in 146 BC. That leaves Polybius, writing about a century after the war, as the main source.
questions.sourceQuote: Carthage's own records perished when the city was destroyed in 146 BC.

questions.question: At which battles is the corvus clearly mentioned in our sources? (select all that apply)
options: Drepana
Ecnomus
Aegates Islands
Mylae
Lipari Islands
questions.explanation: The corvus is clearly mentioned only at Mylae and Ecnomus, then vanishes. Some think its weight made ships top-heavy in storms.
questions.sourceQuote: It is clearly mentioned only at Mylae and Ecnomus, then vanishes.

questions.question: What happened on Rome's first naval venture, a raid on the Lipari Islands?
options: Every ship was captured, along with the consul
The ships ran aground on the Sicilian coast
The crews mutinied and sailed home
The fleet was wrecked by a storm
The consul won a small but famous victory
questions.explanation: Carthaginian ships trapped the 17 Roman ships in harbour at night, and the raw crews panicked. Every ship and the consul himself were captured.
questions.sourceQuote: The raw crews panicked, and every ship was captured, along with the consul himself.

questions.question: What did the king of Syracuse do in 263 BC when facing 40,000 Romans?
options: Fled to Carthage with his treasury
Paid Rome to leave Sicily
Switched sides and agreed to feed Rome's army
Fought a pitched battle and was killed
Invited a Carthaginian garrison into Syracuse
questions.explanation: Syracuse, the strongest Greek city on Sicily, switched sides and agreed to supply Rome's army. Earlier it had been pressing the Mamertines at Messana.
questions.sourceQuote: In 263 BC, facing 40,000 Romans, the king of Syracuse switched sides and agreed to feed Rome's army.

questions.question: What mistake did the overconfident Carthaginians make at the Battle of Mylae?
options: They attacked at night in a storm
They left their rams in harbour
They rushed in without keeping formation
They waited too long to engage
They split their fleet in two
questions.explanation: Sure of their skill, the Carthaginians charged in without formation and were grappled by the ravens. Their flagship's commander escaped in a small boat.
questions.sourceQuote: Sure of their skill, the Carthaginians rushed in without keeping formation.
